title: Siegard plan node
description: One node of a development plan: the frontmatter of one markdown file under the work root. The path is the identity — `inventory/<slug>.md`, `epic/<slug>.md`, `task/<epic>/<slug>.md` — so no id, type or epic field exists to disagree with it. `kind` is supplied by the validator from the path and is never written in a file; the examples omit it the same way. A plan node deliberately carries no status, estimate, priority or order field: execution state lives in git, and order is derived from dependencies by whoever executes — a plan that records progress is an orchestrator's state file, which this framework refuses to have. What the knowledge base leaves open reaches a task as `unresolved` — an open gap of a bound node, cited as `<node-id>#<field>`, or a question no node answers — and the validator requires every open gap on every bound node to be either unresolved or waived: silence over a gap is refused. One example per kind sits in that kind's branch. The body below the frontmatter carries exactly two headings, `## What it is` and `## Notes`.

kind.description: Supplied by the validator from the file path; never written in frontmatter.

summary.description: One sentence saying what the node holds, not what kind it is.

rationale.description: Why the planning decided this. Present means the planning decided; absent means the scope or the base stated it.

sources.description: Where this node was read from — ordinarily files under the work root's `intake/`, which the validator never reads.

area.description: The paths the survey walked, as the caller named the target source root — the root itself when the survey walked all of it. Required even when the target is empty: a greenfield area is a full answer, said in `summary`, and this field still records where the survey looked.

modules.description: What already exists where the change lands. Absent when the area holds nothing.

conventions.description: How the existing code does things, each with the path it was seen at. A convention without evidence is an opinion, and opinions are not inventory.

must_not_duplicate.description: What the plan's tasks must reuse rather than rewrite, each with where it sits.

risks.description: What the change could break, each with the consumers that would observe it. A risk with no named consumer is a worry, not a risk.

covers.description: The base nodes this epic answers for, in both directions: the validator requires every entry to be bound by one of the epic's tasks or declared in `uncovered` — a covered node reaches a task or a stated why, never neither — and refuses a task binding outside this list, because a binding outside the claim is scope the plan does not declare. Two epics may cover the same base node — overlap is shared scope declared, never an error — and each reconciles its own claim independently.

uncovered.description: The deliberate remainder of `covers`: base nodes this epic claims and this plan leaves untouched, each with why. An entry here that a task nevertheless binds is a contradiction the validator refuses.

objective.description: The one falsifiable outcome this task delivers. Two outcomes are two tasks.

criteria.description: The conditions under which the objective counts as met, each falsifiable on its own. "Works correctly" is prose; "a rejected order returns the stated domain error" is a criterion.

depends_on.description: Tasks whose delivered outcome this one builds on. Dependency, never order: the validator refuses a cycle, and any schedule satisfying these edges is equally valid.

produces.description: The artifacts this task's delivery must create, by path relative to the target source root. It is the checkable half of an objective rather than a second statement of it, and it exists because two things read it. A delivery refuses an implementation record whose `files` does not list what the task said it would produce, so the claim is held to what was written rather than to what was meant. And a task producing anything is one building what the project's own standard presupposes — the manifest, the compiler configuration, the artifact a rule names and no rule can ask for — which is why writing source over an absent presupposition stops for every other task and never for this one: holding the task that builds the substrate to the substrate's presence is circular, and the deadlock has no other exit. Ordinary work declares none.
produces.$comment: Held against the implementation record's `files` by bin/deliver.py, and read by /implement-task before anything is written.

nodes.description: The base nodes that govern this task, each with the digest of the node as this binding read it. This is the binding: the executor reads exactly these, and every entry sits inside the epic's `covers` — a task needing more grows the claim or moves. A task that binds nothing is ungoverned by the base and must say why in `rationale`; it carries no digest, because it read nothing.

unresolved.description: What this task needs and the base leaves open. A gap entry cites an open gap on a bound node; a question entry records a fact no node answers. Either way the answer is produced in the base, by /analyse-domain — a task never closes a gap.

waived.description: Open gaps on bound nodes that do not bear on this task, each with why. The waiver is the recorded judgment that makes the validator's totality check honest: every open gap on a bound node is unresolved or waived, never silently ignored.

examples.title: Order service
examples.summary: The area the checkout scope lands in: one layered service under src/.

conventions.statement: Route handlers stay thin and delegate to a service module.

risks.risk: The billing client is shared; a signature change ripples.

examples.title: Checkout
examples.summary: Everything order placement needs, from recording to refusal.

uncovered.why: State handling ships with the follow-up scope; nothing in this plan transitions an order.

examples.title: Record a placed order
examples.summary: The entry point that persists a valid order.
examples.objective: A valid order submitted to the service is persisted and retrievable by its order_number.
criteria: Submitting a valid order returns its order_number.
An order with a non-positive total is refused with the stated rule.

unresolved.question: The scope does not say whether submission is idempotent per order_number.

waived.why: This task only records orders; cancellation is not on its path.

slug.description: A name reduced to kebab-case. A name that will not reduce is a refusal, not a transliteration.

baseNodeRef.description: A knowledge-base node, by identifier — the node's file path under the knowledge root, without `.md`.

boundNode.description: One node of the binding: which base node governs this task, and which version of it the binding read. The pair sits in one entry rather than in two parallel lists, so a node and its digest cannot come apart. A digest the validator finds diverging names this node and no other — that is the point of carrying it per node instead of one value over the whole base, which said only that something somewhere had moved.

digest.description: The node as this binding read it, taken from the `digest` its entry carries in the base's derived graph.json and computable by hand as `sha256sum <knowledge-root>/<node>.md`. Diverging, it says this node moved after the binding — the task is re-bound, or the digest restated deliberately. Two entries naming one node are refused however their digests differ: a binding says once which version it read.

taskRef.description: A task of this plan, by identifier.

gapRef.description: One open gap of one base node: the node's identifier, `#`, and the gap's `field` exactly as the node declares it. The validator holds the reference to a gap the base still has open.

pin.description: Content identity: the SHA-256 of the bytes of whatever artifact the field carrying it names, written `sha256:<hexdigest>` and computable by hand with `sha256sum`. A pin records which version of that artifact a judgment read, so an artifact that moved afterwards is visible to the validator rather than assumed unchanged. The field names the artifact; this is what the value means.

role.description: Whether the change lands in it, leans on it, or merely sits next to it.

seen_at.description: The path the convention was observed at.

question.description: A fact this task needs that no base node holds — the signal to take the scope back to /analyse-domain, never a blank the plan fills.
